headline: Quiet days in the Hub let my blood pressure finally settle
morning_brew: Not much happening on the field today, so let me tell you about the time I watched the Bruins clinch the Cup back in 2011. I was over at Uncle Carmine's place in Revere, and the air in that living room was thicker than the clam chowdah at the local diner. Carmine had his feet up and was snoring like a chainsaw through the entire second period, swearing up and down he was just resting his eyes to see the final horn. I did not wake him until Tim Thomas made that final stop and the boys hoisted the hardware, and to this day, he insists he saw every single save.

Carmine's living room smelled like the cigars he keeps hidden from my aunt, and the couch was covered in that plastic wrap that sticks to your legs if you sit for more than five minutes. My aunt had a tray of ziti sitting on the counter that nobody dared touch until the final whistle blew, because you do not mess with superstition when the B's are playing for the Cup. It was one of those nights where time just stands still, and even though Carmine missed the middle, he still talks like he was coaching the squad from his recliner.

We have a few days of calm before the B's get back to the ice at TD Garden on Saturday to face the Capitals, which gives me plenty of time to stop obsessing over the power rankings. The C's are also heading out west for a Saturday night tilt against the Kings, and hopefully, both squads use this little break to find their focus. I am gonna use the quiet to let my blood pressure recover before the weekend slate kicks off, because we all know the stress is coming back the second the puck drops.
